processing: Orthodox black tea in whole-leaf and tippy grades such as FTGFOP1, with CTC grades also made.
harvest_season: Second flush is the main picking on sale, with autumn flush orthodox lots also offered.
appearance_dry: Dark twisted leaf, heavy with golden tips in the special lots.
taste_profile: Deep malt and full body, with sweetness from the golden tips in the better lots.

brewing.notes: Western-style. It holds up to milk, but tippy lots are worth trying plain first.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush: dated second flush specials and autumn flush orthodox lots, for example 2024 releases. Limited tippy lots cost much more than regular FTGFOP1. As with other orthodox Assams, drink within a year or two.
description:
Nahorhabi is an Assam garden in Sivasagar district, reported to lie near the Nagaland border. It is a regular on estate-tea lists, in plain and very tippy versions alike.

The garden makes both orthodox and CTC. The orthodox lots are the ones sold by name, usually as FTGFOP1 or as limited golden-tip selections.

In the cup it follows the class closely: deep malt, a full body and some sweetness when there is plenty of tip. It is a straightforward tea to brew if you stick to about three minutes in hot water and take it with milk if you enjoy that.

The real choice is between flushes. Second flush is the full, classic style, while autumn lots are a different seasonal character that is worth comparing yourself. Little is written about them beyond sellers' notes.
history: Little is documented about the garden's early years. A seller's account says Jayshree Tea and Industries acquired it in 1955, and the company still lists dated lots from it.
